external_narratives.summary: Imperial War Museums register entry for the memorial to the crew of Blenheim V5851 at Stow Bedon, Norfolk. Records the crash of the 21 Squadron aircraft three miles south of its base at RAF Watton.
external_narratives.key_details: Crew: Sgt F.G.B. Heron (pilot, RCAF, age 20), F/Sgt G.D. Maluish (observer, RCAF, age 23), Sgt G.E. Step (air gunner, RAF, age 20). An eyewitness reported the pilot deliberately put the nose down to avoid hitting a nearby house.

memorial_details:
Grey (probably slate), rectangular tablet mounted at a shallow angle on a low brick plinth. The memorial is surrounded by grey granite chippings contained within low rectangular kerbstones. The dedication is incised in white upper-case letters. The outline of a Bristol Blenheim is incised in the top-left corner with the 21 Squadron badge in the top-right.

A memorial was placed at the crash site in 2000 to honor these young airmen.

Memorial placement (2000): Memorial placed on site in 2000
narrative: On July 7, 1942, a Bristol Blenheim, V5851, belonging to 21 Squadron RAF, crashed near Stow Bedon. The aircraft was piloted by Sergeant F.G.B. Heron, aged 20, with Flight Sergeant G.D. Maluish as air observer and Sergeant G.E. Step as air gunner, both aged 23. Despite the impending danger, an eyewitness noted that the pilot deliberately lowered the plane's nose, crashing into a field to avoid a nearby house. The courage of these men prevented a potential tragedy for the house's inhabitants.
inscription:
IN MEMORY OF
SGT. F.G.B. HERON PILOT RCAF AGED 20
FLT. SGT. G.D. MALUISH AIR OBSERVER RCAF AGED 23
SGT. G.E. STEP AIR GUNNER RAF AGED 20
THESE MEN, ALL OF 21 SQUADRON, RAF WATTON
WERE KILLED WHEN THEIR BRISTOL BLENHEIM, V5851
CRASHED NEAR THIS SPOT ON 7TH JUly 1942
"AN EYEWITNESS REPORTED THAT THE BLENHEIM
WAS FLYING STRAIGHT FOR THIS HOUSE AND THAT THE PILOT PUT THE NOSE DOWN CRASHING INTO THE FIELD.
BUT FOR THE COURAGE OF THESE MEN EVERYONE IN THE HOUSE WOULD HAVE PERISHED.
(poem by Stephen Spender)
